articles.title: Ibac charges police officer accused of repeatedly hitting Indigenous man with Taser during Melbourne arrest
articles.excerpt:
Victorian corruption watchdog alleges weapon was used to hit man’s head, with another officer accused of kneeing him in same incident last year

Two Victorian police officers have been charged with as...
articles.body_text:
Victorian corruption watchdog alleges weapon was used to hit man’s head, with another officer accused of kneeing him in same incident last year

Two Victorian police officers have been charged with assault after allegedly using a Taser and knee to repeatedly strike a man in the head during an arrest last year.

But the officers remain on duty, police have confirmed.

In a statement, the Independent Broad-based Anti-corruption Commission said it had charged the two officers after an investigation into the force used during an arrest of an Indigenous man in Melbourne’s east last August.

“During the arrest, it is alleged [a] Senior Constable unlawfully struck the man to the head with a taser multiple times,” Ibac said.

“They have been charged with aggravated assault with a weapon.

“In addition, it is alleged the Sergeant unlawfully struck the man to the head with their knee. They have been charged with unlawful assault.”

Both officers are expected to appear before the Ringwood magistrates court on 11 September.

Victoria police said in a statement that the officers were charged on Wednesday and that all further enquiries should be directed to IBAC.

“The members continue to work in their current roles,” police said.

The Ibac investigation, codenamed Operation Ginkgo, was conducted by the focused police complaints team (FPCT).

“IBAC’s FPCT assesses and investigates serious, single-incident allegations of Victoria Police misconduct against people from communities at a higher risk of experiencing police misconduct, including First Nations people,” Ibac said.

“As the matter is now before the court, no further information is available.”

Ibac says the team is responsible for an increase in the number of complaints it investigates involving police.

But data released in March showed the commission investigated just 2% of all complaints it received regarding police last year.

articles.title: Australian army whistleblower released on parole after more than two years in jail
articles.excerpt:
David McBride pleaded guilty to leaking military secrets to the media in 2023

A whistleblower jailed for leaking military secrets about Australia's involvement in Afghanistan has been released on par...
articles.body_text:
David McBride pleaded guilty to leaking military secrets to the media in 2023

A whistleblower jailed for leaking military secrets about Australia's involvement in Afghanistan has been released on parole after serving 27 months.

In 2024, David McBride was sentenced to five years and eight months after pleading guilty to stealing top secret defence documents and giving it to the media.

His actions later led to a landmark inquiry that found evidence that Australian forces had unlawfully killed 39 Afghans during the war.

On Thursday, a spokesperson for the Attorney-General Michelle Rowland said McBride's "parole was considered and granted". The ex-military lawyer, who is being treated for lung cancer, will serve the rest of his sentence in the community under supervision.

Shortly after the decision, advocacy group The Information Rights Project released a statement on McBride's behalf, according to national broadcaster ABC.

He thanked his family "who never gave up on me and whose fighting spirit, love and humour inspired me every day" and praised "all my amazing supporters from around both Australia and the world who sent me such inspirational messages".

McBride also revealed that he had been diagnosed with treatable lung cancer and would be having surgery to remove part of his lung.

His lawyer Edwina Lloyd described the decision to grant his parole as "the right one", in a statement according to the ABC.

She said McBride's life has been "defined by service to Australia", both as a legal officer for the Australian Defence Forces (ADF) and having served time for his crimes.

During his court case, prosecutors argued that McBride's actions had been motivated by "personal vindication", and that the way he gathered, stored and then leaked the documents endangered Australia's national security and foreign policy.

But McBride's lawyers asked for leniency, saying he shared the information with "honourable" intentions and out of a sense of personal duty.

In sentencing McBride, the judge said while he was of "good character", sharing military secrets was a "gross breach of trust" and he had shown "no contrition" for his actions.

The material he leaked to the ABC underpinned a series of reports in 2017 called The Afghan Files which provided unprecedented insight into Australia's elite special forces in Afghanistan, including allegations of war crimes.

In 2020, the Brereton Report found "credible evidence" that elite soldiers have unlawfully killed 39 people.

A special watchdog - the Office of the Special Investigator - was set up to look into the actions of 19 ADF members. Of its 53 cases, 39 have been finalised and two former Special Air Service (SAS) soldiers have been charged.

Ben Roberts-Smith, Australia's most decorated living soldier, is facing five counts of the war crime of murder after he was charged earlier this year, while Oliver Schulz faces one count of the same charge.

articles.title: Telstra CEO gets $700,000 pay rise to $6.8m despite Australia-wide outage
articles.excerpt:
Telco board cuts senior executive bonuses by total $1.3m after tech fail that affected millions

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily ...
articles.body_text:
Telco board cuts senior executive bonuses by total $1.3m after tech fail that affected millions

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Telstra has paid its chief executive, Vicki Brady, $6.8m for the year ending in June, after docking 20% of her bonus in response to the network’s nationwide outage in July.

The company reported financial results on Thursday. Its board met on Monday and decided to cut Brady’s bonus by $607,000 – but she still took home a $700,000 pay rise as she was awarded a total of $6.1m the year before.

Telstra has faced heavy political criticism for its handling of the outage, which it has blamed on the lack of a software update on a key time-keeping system. The incident was estimated to have affected almost half of all calls and data sessions on its network before it was traced and repaired.

Brady told investors on Thursday more than 30,000 customers had asked for compensation and nearly $1m had been paid out. The company reported it was still assessing customer claims, and was paying compensation to those who were eligible.

“At this stage regulatory outcomes and any financial implications from this outage are uncertain and cannot be reliably estimated,” the financial report read.

Brady acknowledged the outage in comments to investors on Thursday, saying that Telstra had “let our customers down in July” and had taken full accountability.

“We have an initial understanding of the root cause of the outage and have taken steps to address that,” she said. “We are completing our investigation with an external expert, and we will be transparent about those findings and the actions we take as a result.”

Brady said the company was taking the disruption “extremely seriously” and was committed to giving people clear information and fixing issues as quickly as possible.

Telstra also docked 20% of the bonus for its former global networks group executive, and 10% of all other senior executives, cutting their combined pay by the equivalent of $1.3m. The company’s results show senior executives were paid a combined $20.7m for the year.

Brady told reporters there was a “small impact” in customers leaving the telco following July’s outage, but ultimately “no material impact” on customers leaving or new customers signing up.

“I don’t take that for granted, nor do any of the team at Telstra.”

Wednesday’s earnings results showed profits rose to $2.4bn, from $2.3bn the prior year. It paid shareholders a dividend of 21 cents per share.

Telstra has cut costs by cutting jobs: employee numbers fell by 1,219 over the year to a total 29,334 by June.

Income from mobile phones rose $300m to $11.3bn, with customers paying an extra 7.2% on prepaid handheld plans and an extra 3.4% on postpaid handheld plans. The company increased most of its postpaid plans by $4 a month and prepaid by $5 a month in May.

Telstra sold 1m more mobile plans despite rising prices and now has 26m services in operation.

However, following multiple price increases, much of the company’s growth in subscribers is being driven through prepaid and its wholesale business, which sells Telstra’s mobile network under brands including Woolworths and Aldi. Brady called this the “value-conscious end of the market”.

Telstra reported a drop in postpaid subscriptions directly with Telstra of 7,000 in the financial year, compared to 46,000 additions in pre-paid, and 235,000 in wholesale.

Brady said the wholesale offers give customers “a lot of choice… because we fully appreciate and understand that cost of living is a big pressure on a lot of people in the country.”

The company’s share price slipped from $5 to $4.875 in early trading, dragging its market value down by $1.4bn to hit $54.3bn.

articles.title: Surrogate mother who fled to Texas gives birth to baby with severe heart defect
articles.excerpt:
McKenna West initially agreed to an abortion after diagnosis, but then fled to state where abortion is illegal and broke contact with biological parents, attorney alleges

A surrogate mother who trave...
articles.body_text:
McKenna West initially agreed to an abortion after diagnosis, but then fled to state where abortion is illegal and broke contact with biological parents, attorney alleges

A surrogate mother who traveled to Texas, where abortion is illegal, claiming she was pressured to end the pregnancy after the discovery of a severe heart defect, gave birth on Wednesday to a baby boy.

The child’s biological parents, Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed of California, confirmed the birth through their lawyer, while denying they forced McKenna West, who is from Alaska, to undergo an abortion, the Texas Tribune reported.

“Our clients’ child was born earlier this morning and he is now receiving medical care provided by a team of pediatric experts,” Lee Budner, an attorney, said in a statement to the Texas Tribune.

In a July filing from an Alaska court, obtained by the outlet, attorneys for Gilkar and Ahmed wrote the couple and West were initially in consensus about an abortion.

The dispute attracted national attention this week, after Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general, intervened in the case on behalf of West. He publicized an emergency court order out of Dallas county, barring the then-fetus from being taken out of state and requesting for area hospitals to provide “life-saving” care.

Texas’s top prosecutors and West maintained the California couple intended to deprive the child of such treatment. The couple has refuted that claim.

The fetus had been diagnosed with a hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a condition that interferes with the body’s ability to pump oxygen-rich blood throughout, which could cause breathing problems.

According to the CDC, soon after birth, children with the congenital heart defect require multiple surgeries completed in a particular order. The procedures, the agency advised on its website, were not a cure. Lifelong complications may persist.

“My office utilized every tool at our disposal to protect life, and we will not back down in continuing to support baby Gabriel’s well-being,” Paxton said in a Tuesday news release, using a name not given by the California couple. “Every child in our state deserves to be cared for and protected, and that’s exactly what I’ll fight for.”

West appeared on conservative media pundit Megyn Kelly’s podcast last week. An agency had contracted her as a surrogate. She said she believed, speaking with the couple, that “if something came up … termination would not be their first choice”.

“I felt very trapped due to this contract. I felt like I had no voice,” West said, referring to a surrogacy agreement. “But I knew in my soul, in my heart that I wanted to protect this little boy.”

Under state law, abortion in Texas is banned under most circumstances, except when a mother’s health is at risk, a clause that has received scrutiny for its vague wording and nebulous enforcement.

Budner characterized West and Paxton’s actions to the Texas Tribune as “political theater”.

“After heartbreaking consultations with medical providers and their own research about the suffering and quality of life HLHS babies endure, A.B. and C.D. made the difficult decision to terminate the pregnancy,” the filing read, referring to Gilkar and Ahmed with anonymized initials. “It is undisputed that West initially agreed and that she herself made the initial appointment. She then unilaterally changed her mind, cut off all contact with A.B. and C.D., and withdrew medical releases allowing A.B. and C.D. to have contact with all medical providers.”

articles.title: Reformers were ‘spectacularly unsuccessful’ in taking over NSW Liberals, Catholic schools boss says
articles.excerpt:
Catholic Schools NSW chief executive Dallas McInerney tells Icac corruption inquiry that Christain factional group driven by ‘a calling … a duty’

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest update...
articles.body_text:
Catholic Schools NSW chief executive Dallas McInerney tells Icac corruption inquiry that Christain factional group driven by ‘a calling … a duty’

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A factional ally of the federal opposition leader, Angus Taylor, has told a corruption inquiry that a group of Christian Liberal power brokers who allegedly solicited illegal political donations were “spectacularly unsuccessful in their ambitions”.

The Catholic Schools NSW chief executive, Dallas McInerney, told the Independent Commission Against Corruption on Thursday that the Reformers’ model was never correct.

Icac is investigating whether McInerney arranged and approved donations from the governing body for 600 Catholic schools to support alleged branch stacking efforts of the conservative Christian group.

The Reformers wanted more conservative policies on issues such as same-sex marriage, abortion and euthanasia. A document drafted around the group’s inception proposed to recruit 5,000 Christian conservatives to join New South Wales Liberal party branches “and thereby take control of the NSW division of the Liberal party”.

McInerney on Thursday admitted he first became aware of Reformers’ recruitment events in late 2018 and 2019. He said he was “mostly” supportive of their goals.

The counsel assisting Juliet Curtin asked: “What’s the qualification here, Mr McInerney?”

“They were spectacularly unsuccessful in their ambitions,” he replied. “I never thought the model was right.”

McInerney stood aside from his role as CEO before the Icac hearings began “to allow the work of Catholic Schools NSW to continue its important mission”, he previously said in a statement.

McInerney on Thursday accepted he had begun to speak frequently to Reformers Christian Ellis, Robert Assaf and Jean-Claude Perrottet by 2020. Asked if he knew that the men were “fervent” in the pursuit of the Reformers’ goals, McInerney said the word was “very subjective”.

Asked if “passionate” was a better word, he said: “I actually don’t think there was a passion there. I think it was a calling for them, a duty.”

Nearly 80% of funding managed by Catholic Schools NSW comes from federal and state funding, or about $3.8bn in 2024.

Icac has previously heard that Catholic Schools NSW paid monthly retainers to two lobbying firms controlled by members of the Reformers for consulting services.

It paid Beckington, run by Ellis and Jeremy Greenwood, $130,900 between August 2019 and August 2021, and JPG Advisory, run by Greenwood, $135,000 between December 2021 and December 2023.

During evidence on Wednesday, Greenwood, who has disputed whether he was a member of the Reformers, was read messages between himself and McInerney in October 2022 in which the latter asked about missing invoices. Greenwood responded: “I stopped sending them in the end haha.”

The counsel assisting Peggy Dwyer SC asked why he had signed off the message in that way: “Is the joke on parents paying funds to Catholic Schools NSW, or the government assisting with that funding, that this money is not for any genuine consultancy, but was in fact intended in part to fund Jean-Claude Perrottet?”

On Thursday, the inquiry heard that McInerney, the only CEO of Catholic Schools NSW since its founding in 2017, joined the Liberal party while at school in the late 1980s or early 1990s. He remained a member until June this year, when he also ceased being the president of the Mittagong branch.

McInerney, a member of the Liberals right faction, came to know senior conservative state and federal parliamentarians including Tony Abbott, Angus Taylor, Matt Canavan, Dominic Perrottet and Damien Tudehope. McInerney and right faction members later spoke at Reformers events.

He said the right faction members had “uniform awareness and knowledge” about the Reformers’ work, but were “not uniformly supportive in acceptance”.

In its first week, the inquiry heard a message sent by McInerney, who is a factional ally of Taylor, to Assaf in March 2021, advising of a plan to “shake down Angus for 10K”.

Taylor has not been named in Icac’s allegations and has repeatedly denied he ever made payments to the Reformers.

McInerney admitted to having his own political ambitions “off and on for several” years, but said he was “at peace” with not taking over the late federal Liberal senator Jim Molan’s seat. Molan died in January 2023 but McInerney missed out on the Senate spot.

He was read messages exchanged between him and Greenwood in which he wrote: “I know I’ve been fucked.”

“Yeah it’s fucked, it’s fucked, it’s fucked,” McInerney wrote in March 2023.

articles.title: Clueless WNBA attacks 'bad-faith' fans who don't want biological men ruining women's sports
articles.excerpt:
DiJonai Carrington is claiming she has evidence as to why she said "white privilege". Okay, so where's the evidence?

The WNBA convened a task force to figure out what a woman is, emerged without an a...
articles.body_text:
DiJonai Carrington is claiming she has evidence as to why she said "white privilege". Okay, so where's the evidence?

The WNBA convened a task force to figure out what a woman is, emerged without an answer, scheduled more meetings to keep figuring it out, then scolded everyone else for the "hate and vitriol" surrounding the debate.

On Wednesday, the WNBA finally offered an update on its progress.

WNBPA ISSUES STATEMENT EMBRACING DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION AMID TRANS ATHLETE DEBATE IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

"Today's meeting covered a wide range of topics, including ongoing discussions on transgender athletes and the continued hate and vitriol directed at players online. We will continue to engage all league stakeholders in the coming weeks and months. We will approach these important conversations thoughtfully and in alignment with the values of our league. There are no immediate eligibility matters affecting the WNBA, and we strongly denounce the bad-faith efforts to use these topics to demean or marginalize others."

The WNBA took the corporate escape hatch. Dodge the question, scold the critics and kick the can down the road.

WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert speaks prior to the 2026 WNBA Draft at The Shed on April 13, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images)

Somewhere in all these meetings is WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert, who runs a women's league that still can't settle on who qualifies as a woman. Quite the predicament.

The loophole gets a lot more complicated to ignore when ex-NBA players Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White declared for the 2027 WNBA Draft just to expose it.

The league's own CBA says "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." Pretty straightforward. Except there's one small problem: nowhere in the 400-plus-page agreement does the WNBA define what a woman is.

While executives spin their wheels in meetings, women willing to defend the purpose of women's sports are left to stand alone. Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has publicly supported keeping women's sports and locker rooms for biological females.

Then, after Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington was ejected for a Flagrant 2 foul for striking Cunningham across the head, Carrington went to social media and posted "WHITE PRIVILEGE @indianafever."

WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert speaks after the 2026 AT&T WNBA All-Star Game at the United Center on July 25, 2026, in Chicago, Ill. (Getty Images)

Fever coach Stephanie White eventually called the hit "egregious," but only after criticism mounted over her initial silence. When she addressed the controversy, much of her response focused on the "online community" and condemning "hate," "fear-mongering" and "divisiveness."

THE WNBA HAS LIMITED OPTIONS AFTER TWO MEN DECLARED FOR THE DRAFT, AND THOSE OPTIONS AREN'T GREAT

That's the recurring problem. Cunningham stands up for female competition, absorbs the backlash and gets hammered on the court, while the people running women's basketball seem more comfortable policing the tone of the debate than standing behind women raising uncomfortable questions.

Meanwhile, global sports bodies like World Aquatics, World Athletics and the UCI have established firm, biological eligibility standards. The WNBA remains stuck in an endless loop of listening sessions, stakeholder engagement and sanitized PR statements. Eventually, the league has to decide what it exists to protect. Stalling with PR spin won't alter basic biology.

Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham celebrates a three-point basket Tuesday, Aug. 11, 2026, during a game at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect)

If the WNBA continues to run meetings instead of making decisions, and lecture critics instead of standing up for women willing to speak, it won't be long before an eligibility disaster makes the decision for them.

OutKick reached out to the WNBA for comment/explanation on what defines a woman. We have not received a response.

Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak on track to be deadliest ever, WHO chief says
articles.excerpt:
The current outbreak of Ebola in the DR Congo is on track to surpass the deadliest outbreak of the disease ever, the director-general of the World Health Organisation (WHO) has said.

Tedros Adhanom G...
articles.body_text:
The current outbreak of Ebola in the DR Congo is on track to surpass the deadliest outbreak of the disease ever, the director-general of the World Health Organisation (WHO) has said.

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told reporters that the 2026 outbreak, "at its current pace", would "eclipse" that of the 2014-2016 occurrence, which killed at least 11,000 people.

The outbreak this year, declared on 15 May, has seen at least 4,300 cases and caused more than 2,000 deaths.

The WHO said on Wednesday it hoped to reverse the spread of the disease within three months but warned that this meant bringing transmission under control - not ending the outbreak entirely.

The epidemic was only officially declared in May, but it is believed the outbreak began at least three months before then, health officials said this week.

"We are chasing the virus, the virus is ahead of us," WHO Africa director Dr Mohamed Janabi said at a news conference in the city of Bunia, near the centre of the outbreak.

He cited research showing that the virus started spreading in February and was initially misdiagnosed as malaria or typhoid.

The 2026 outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which has previously caused only two known outbreaks - in 2007 and 2012.

No approved vaccine or recognised therapeutic drugs can treat this species of the virus.

Ongoing regional instability near the location of the outbreak, in the east of the DR Congo, has added to challenges in controlling the spread of the disease. As a result, health workers are only reaching about 30% of cases, according to Janabi.

Ebola is a rare but deadly viral disease, with symptoms appearing within two to 21 days of infection.

Symptoms similar to the flu or malaria, including fever, headache and tiredness, can begin suddenly. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea can develop, leading to organ failure.

The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

The UK's medicines regulator, the MHRA, has given permission for the first human trials of a vaccine for Bundibugyo to go ahead.

The jab is being created by a team from the University of Oxford based on the same technology used in the Oxford-AstraZeneca Covid vaccine. Three other groups are also developing different vaccines for Bundibugyo although they have not yet entered clinical trials.

The WHO is also sponsoring a separate clinical trial in the DR Congo to see whether two existing antiviral therapies can improve survival rates.

We are chasing Ebola virus - it is ahead of us, WHO warns

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

How health workers in DR Congo are treating Ebola and staying safe

articles.title: Travis Kelce shares first details from his wedding to Taylor Swift - 'Best night of my life'
articles.excerpt:
American football player Travis Kelce has reflected on his wedding to Taylor Swift, telling US media that their nuptials were "the best night of my life".

Kelce and Swift tied the knot on 3 July at N...
articles.body_text:
American football player Travis Kelce has reflected on his wedding to Taylor Swift, telling US media that their nuptials were "the best night of my life".

Kelce and Swift tied the knot on 3 July at New York's Madison Square Garden in a star-studded event that was largely kept private.

Few details from the ceremony have been shared publicly and Kelce's comments on Wednesday mark the first he's shared since the couple were wed by comedic actor Adam Sandler.

"It was kind of cool to live out my childhood dream of being in that venue, the mecca of all sports venues, being able to get married there," Kelce told reporters at the Kansas City Chiefs' training camp in Missouri.

Kelce called the wedding "the best night of my life", thanking guests who attended and calling it "a crazy night".

The NFL star and the award-winning singer have kept much of the details of the wedding private and there have been no official photos released of the ceremony held inside the stadium. A litany of Hollywood A-list stars, such as actors Hugh Grant and Jason Sudeikis, singer Benson Boone and model Gigi Hadid were in attendance.

Kelce said he had wanted to attend a game when the New York Knicks basketball team were having a good playoff run last year, but had other commitments. The team ended up winning the NBA championships for the first time in nearly six decades.

"My wife went when I was stuck in a mini camp so I didn't get my opportunity to go then," he said referring to Swift as his wife publicly for the first time. She sat courtside at Game 4 of the NBA Finals, when the Knicks pulled off a stunning upset against the San Antonio Spurs in a 107-106 finish.

In pictures: Stars and fans celebrate Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's wedding

From 'a beautiful night' to 'world's greatest hangover', guests react to Taylor and Travis's wedding

"I can't thank the owners of MSG enough for allowing us to get the opportunity to do that, knowing that we wanted a private event and everything, and it was perfect," he added.

Later, he joked that the "AC was cooking" inside the venue, an apparent reference to the heatwave that swept over the country over the Independence Day weekend.

The couple's nuptials were shrouded in secrecy despite the event shutting down a part of New York City - the most populous city in the US. Much of the event still was wrapped in uncertainty as to whether the couple had already wed in days prior or whether the event might just be a party.

But hours after a lengthy list of celebrities were seen entering the venue in gowns and suits, large screens attached to the arena announced publicly that the famous couple were officially wed.

Kelce noted "it was a fun off-season" but said he was now excited to return to training and American football.

Kelce, who turns 37 in October, has won three Super Bowl championships with the Chiefs.

The team did not make the NFL playoffs last year for the first time in 10 seasons. Many believe the upcoming season, which begins next month, could be his last. But the tight end hasn't said whether retirement could be next.

"I have still got a lot of love for this game," he said. "I want to go out there and prove to myself that I can play at a better level than I did last year."

"This is always going to be my sanctuary," he said of being back on the field. "You need to have this time of grinding with the guys, being around them all day, starting to create that chemistry and standard for how we are going to do things. This year it's ramped up even more.

From friendship bracelets to wedding rings: A Taylor and Travis timeline

Taylor Swift marries Travis Kelce in NYC ceremony officiated by Adam Sandler

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

David...
articles.body_text:
Attorney general grants former army lawyer’s release after 27 months in jail

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

David McBride, the former army lawyer jailed for his role in stealing secret defence documents about the Afghanistan war and leaking them to the media, has been released from prison in Canberra on Thursday.

McBride was sentenced to a maximum five years and eight months in jail in May 2024, but is being released on parole after serving his full non-parole period of 27 months.

McBride pleaded guilty to three charges in November after the ACT supreme court upheld a commonwealth intervention to withhold key evidence the government argued had the potential to jeopardise “the security and defence of Australia”. The charges included stealing commonwealth information and passing that on to journalists at the ABC.

The attorney general, Michelle Rowland, approved McBride’s release on Thursday.

A spokesperson for Rowland confirmed his release to Guardian Australia.

“Mr McBride’s parole was considered and granted,” the spokesperson said.

“The government does not provide specific commentary or details about individual parole matters.”

McBride released a statement after the decision, thanking Rowland “for sparing us another long fight over the question of parole.”

“After all we both want the same thing, a better Australia for our children, so it seems a waste to be fighting each other, rather than working together,” he said.

He said he would make a more comprehensive statement at a later date and acknowledged his family, prison officers and his fellow inmates.

McBride also revealed he was diagnosed with treatable lung cancer, currently in its early stages. He is expected to undergo surgery imminently.

“Many thanked me for allowing them to believe in this country again, in turn, I thank them for showing me there are so many good people in the world worth fighting for,” he said.

McBride collected mostly secret military information over an 18-month period in 2014 and 2015 and handed it to journalists at the public broadcaster. The material was used as the basis for an investigative series exposing war crimes committed by Australian defence personnel in Afghanistan titled The Afghan Files.

The court heard a total of 235 documents were taken by McBride from defence offices – mostly in the ACT – between May 2014 and December 2015 with 207 of them classified as secret and some marked as cabinet documents.

Former independent senator and transparency campaigner Rex Patrick said McBride would walk away from prison with his head held high.

“David served Australians, both in the Army and in his brave act of blowing the whistle on war crimes that took place in Afghanistan. It’s so good to see the end of an awful saga that should never have happened.”

The Information Rights Project founder, Gabriel Shipton, praised the government for the decision, as well as for assistance provided to his brother, Julian Assange.

“David shouldn’t have gone to prison in the first place, but freeing a whistleblower will not go un-noticed,” Shipton said.

“It’s real-world outcomes like these that make a difference to the lives of courageous individuals who blow the whistle. A massive shout-out to all those who supported David through his epic battle for justice.”

articles.title: Rubio rejects RFK's 'crazy' diet, jokes Pop-Tarts are 'one of the great American innovations'
articles.excerpt:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his wife, Jeanette, were asked about their thoughts on the "Make America Healthy Again" movement on Katie Millers podcast.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio jokingly p...
articles.body_text:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his wife, Jeanette, were asked about their thoughts on the "Make America Healthy Again" movement on Katie Millers podcast.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio jokingly proclaimed his love of Pop-Tarts while rejecting Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s diet during an interview with podcast host Katie Miller on Tuesday.

Rubio appeared with his wife, Jeanette, on "The Katie Miller Podcast", during which Miller asked his thoughts about Kennedy's reported diet of "red meat and fermented vegetables."

"This is a crazy diet," Rubio said in jest. "This is a diet that consists of eating sauerkraut and meat. Now you understand, like, this is not a sustainable thing ... He has to travel with coolers of sauerkraut! I'm not going to travel the world with a cooler full of sauerkraut. It's ridiculous. I can't do it."

HOW MARCO RUBIO IS RIDING LAUGHTER AND MEMES TO SOCIAL MEDIA DOMINANCE

Marco Rubio and his wife Jeanette appeared on Katie Miller's podcast. (Screenshot/Katie Miller Podcast)

During the exchange, Rubio clarified that he was in favor of Kennedy's "MAHA," or "Make America Healthy Again" movement, though his wife pushed back, claiming that he eats Pop-Tarts.

"No, I don't eat Pop-Tarts every day," Rubio said.

"The Pop-Tart is one of the great American innovations in the history of the world, if you think about it. It comes in this beautiful foil package," Rubio joked.

"He eats all the things you should not be eating. Like every single thing," Jeanette insisted.

MARCO RUBIO ADDRESSES UAP GOVERNMENT COVER-UP ALLEGATIONS, SAYS TRUMP WOULD GIVE A SPEECH IF ADMIN KNEW MORE

Marco Rubio addressed past jokes at his expense from a viral meme on Fox News. (Alain Jocrad/AFP via Getty Images)

Fox News Digital reached out to the HHS secretary and Mars Inc., the company that owns Pop-Tarts, for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Rubio has been considered a potential 2028 presidential candidate to succeed President Donald Trump. In a recent New Hampshire poll, Rubio was only 10 points behind Vice President JD Vance in a hypothetical match-up.

In addition to being a presidential contender, Rubio was also the subject of a viral internet meme featuring him sitting on an Oval Office couch during Trump's meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in 2025.

RUBIO REFLECTS ON REMARKABLE POLITICAL JOURNEY FROM TRUMP CRITIC TO TRUSTED CABINET MEMBER

Secretary of State Marco Rubio has been considered a potential 2028 presidential candidate. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

Rubio finally addressed the viral image in an interview on Fox News' "My View with Lara Trump" last month.

"The meme thing, it was interesting because when it first came out, I hated that picture," Rubio said. "Because what happened is in that couch, if you don’t have a pillow behind your back, you kind of sink.  So, I looked at the picture; I said, ‘Oh, this is terrible,’ I looked like whatever. And then it turned into this other thing. And it was fine, and it’s funny."

"I don’t really follow it very closely, but people have shown me pictures out there," he added. "We have a good friend here that works at the White House, Dan Scavino, made a nice board for me. And even since he made that board, we had to update it, so — of all the different pictures. So that stuff is funny."

Lindsay Kornick is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to lindsay.kornick@fox.com and on Twitter: @lmkornick.

articles.title: Convicted rapist who preyed on women at America's top party school faces reckoning after courthouse dash
articles.excerpt: Emily Compagno, Kayleigh McEnany, Harris Faulkner, and Steve Doocy discuss the arrest of Israel Christopher Flores-Ortiz (19), an illegal immigrant from El Salvador, accused of groping 12 female high ...
articles.body_text:
Emily Compagno, Kayleigh McEnany, Harris Faulkner, and Steve Doocy discuss the arrest of Israel Christopher Flores-Ortiz (19), an illegal immigrant from El Salvador, accused of groping 12 female high school classmates in Fairfax County, Virginia. The Outnumbered panel slams the school district for allegedly covering up the assaults for weeks, violating state law. They also criticize the Biden administration's immigration policies, which allowed him to enter illegally in 2024.

A former UC Santa Barbara student convicted of raping and sexually assaulting multiple women will spend at least three decades behind bars, capping a yearslong prosecution involving disturbing allegations of sexual violence at one of America's top party schools.

Arian Eteghaei, 24, was sentenced to 30 years to life in California state prison after a jury found him guilty of forcible rape and forcible sexual penetration, but not before authorities say he made a brazen run for freedom, bolting from courthouse custody moments after his conviction.

His sentencing comes amid renewed scrutiny over sexual violence at UC Santa Barbara, which has been ranked the nation's top party school by Niche for the past two years.

Eteghaei's case adds to those concerns. He was also convicted of misdemeanor domestic violence, while jurors found true a special allegation that the sexual offenses were committed against more than one victim.

AMERICA'S TOP PARTY COLLEGE HIT BY ANOTHER SEX ATTACK WEEKS AFTER BRUTAL CAMPUS RAPE CASE

"This case would not have been possible without the extraordinary courage of the victims who came forward and participated in a long and difficult legal process," Santa Barbara County District Attorney John T. Savrnoch said. "Their strength and willingness to testify allowed the truth to be heard and ultimately allowed the defendant to be held accountable for the serious harm he caused."

Authorities say Eteghaei escaped by force while in custody on Jan. 16, the same day the jury returned its verdict.

The alleged escape landed Eteghaei another felony case, with prosecutors charging him in March with one count of escape by force.

STUDENTS AT TOP PARTY COLLEGE ON EDGE AFTER RAPE, STRANGULATION REPORTED IN CAMPUS HOUSING

Students walk on the University of California, Santa Barbara campus in Santa Barbara, Calif. (Kevin Koeppen Photography / Getty Images, File)

Eteghaei's sexual assault prosecution stretched back years and centered on crimes committed while he was a student at UC Santa Barbara.

"This case required years of persistence, careful investigation, and tremendous support for the victims," Savrnoch said. "The collective work of this team exemplifies the commitment of law enforcement, prosecutors, investigators, and victim advocates to seeking justice for survivors of sexual violence."

Campus crime data previously reviewed by Fox News Digital show more than 100 reported rapes between 2022 and 2024, while two separate sexual assault reports this spring and summer prompted campus-wide warnings and heightened concerns about student safety.

In June, UC Santa Barbara police issued a campus-wide Timely Warning after a woman reported being stalked and groped in broad daylight near Tierra De Fortuna Park.

RIDESHARE DRIVER ARRESTED IN ALLEGED SCHEME TARGETING IVY LEAGUE STUDENTS FOR SEX: PROSECUTORS

Police said the woman was walking along a paved access road on UCSB's West Campus around 11:30 a.m. June 24, when a man riding a bicycle passed her before circling back multiple times over the next 15 minutes.

During the first two encounters, police said the man stopped to ask her questions. On the third pass, investigators said he approached the woman from behind, groped her and fled toward nearby Tierra De Fortuna Park.

The incident marked the second Timely Warning issued by UCSB police in under two months.

In May, an 18-year-old freshman reported she was raped and strangled after meeting a man at a fraternity party before returning to her dorm at Tropicana Gardens in Isla Vista.

FORMER UCLA GYNECOLOGIST SENTENCED AFTER PLEADING GUILTY TO SEXUALLY ASSAULTING PATIENTS AT SCHOOL

UC Santa Barbara freshman Elizabeth "Liz" Hamel died after a fall from a campus residence hall in February 2025; police ruled it an accident, but the district attorney’s office says the case remains under review. (Marli Miller/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Days after the attack, the survivor's family, through attorney Tyrone Maho, publicly appealed for witnesses to come forward, saying anyone who attended the fraternity party or was near Tropicana Gardens on the night of May 9 could hold critical information.

The family also urged the university's chancellor to ask the Santa Barbara County Sheriff's Office to take over the investigation, arguing that the unidentified attacker remained "a potential threat to our community," while expressing gratitude for the work already done by UC Santa Barbara police.

The attack prompted a candlelight vigil where students gathered to support the survivor and raise concerns about campus safety.

UC Santa Barbara has been ranked the nation's top party school by Niche for the past two years.

TEACHER WHO SERVED AS GOP STATE LAWMAKER ALLEGEDLY USED ROBLOX TO LURE STUDENT INTO SEXUAL RELATIONSHIP

Walkway and Storke Tower are shown on the University of California at Santa Barbara campus. (Marli Miller/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Campus crime data previously reviewed by Fox News Digital showed the university recorded more than 100 reported rapes between 2022 and 2024, according to its Annual Security and Fire Safety Reports.

The reports also showed increases in other reported crimes in recent years, including weapons arrests and burglaries.

In a statement previously provided to Fox News Digital following the May attack, UC Santa Barbara police said federal law limits what officials can disclose about active investigations, but emphasized that reports of crimes on university property are fully investigated by sworn officers.

The department said it remained in direct contact with the survivor's family and works closely with the Santa Barbara County Sheriff's Office and District Attorney's Office when appropriate.

Fox News Digital reached out to the UCSB for comment, but did not immediately receive a response.

Fox News Digital's Kelsie Cairns contributed to this report.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

articles.body_text:
The roof is collapsing on the Democrat establishment — and the inmates are now running the asylum. George Conway gets blown out by a "Team CDC" candidate, the DCCC fumbles Matt Dunlap's résumé in Maine, and a fresh crop of DSA primary winners is heading to Washington and Albany with the wildest platforms you've ever heard.

Republican congressional candidate and Grammy-nominated composer Marty O'Donnell spoke to Fox News Digital on Wednesday about how he was disinvited from a reunion with his fellow creators of the "Halo" video game series for comments made on the campaign trail.

On Tuesday, O’Donnell shared a screenshot of an email he received from his booker who handles his event appearances, informing him he had been uninvited from a reunion of his fellow "Halo" creators at a pop culture convention, saying, "The promoter for SacAnime has shared that his LGBTQ staff does not feel comfortable if you attend the event. Based on your recently reported statements of the political campaign, they have rescinded their invitation to not cause any further staff upset."

"I’m very disappointed that SacAnime has disinvited me from a Halo 25 reunion at their conference next month. If you thought we defeated Cancel Culture in 2024, guess again!" O’Donnell responded in a tweet.

O’Donnell spent decades creating some of the most iconic music in video game history. He has since thrown his hat in the ring as the Trump-backed Republican nominee to represent Nevada's 3rd Congressional District. O’Donnell shared a statement about the incident with Fox News Digital on Wednesday.

GAMING-WORLD VETERAN WHO RIPPED ‘WOKE’ CULTURE SCORES TRUMP-BACKED BATTLEGROUND PRIMARY WIN

Marty O'Donnell revealed on Tuesday that he had been uninvited from a pop culture convention's special reunion event for the team behind the "Halo" franchise due to outrage over a recent comment on a podcast. (Ruthless Podcast)

"In January, I was invited to attend a Halo reunion at SacAnime over Labor Day weekend in Sacramento, CA. I was excited to attend with so many stars, including Jen Taylor and Steve Down[e]s, to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Halo with all of our fans. They even asked me to record a video promoting my attendance two weeks ago," he recalled.

"After SacAnime made numerous announcements of my attendance over this last weekend, I was told I was being disinvited because I called Marxism an existential threat. They have removed me from their website and deleted all their posts on social media promoting my appearance," O'Donnell continued.

"My existential threat comment has been twisted a lot by my political opponents over the last few weeks and anyone who saw the video knows that to be true," he added. "That is why I know it’s not why I have been pulled from SacAnime. I was pulled because I am a Republican candidate for office."

"Funny enough, SacAnime’s decision proves my point. Silencing the opposition is a key component of Marxism and that is one reason why Marxism is an existential threat to our country," O’Donnell said. "I genuinely believed we had put an end to Cancel Culture after the 2024 election, but that was just the end to what AOC called ‘Woke 1’ earlier this week. Woke 2 is here, and it is just as eager to silence and destroy conservatives as Woke 1."

"Unfortunately for them, I can’t be silenced. I will continue to use my voice to speak out against the threats our country faces, especially from Marxists who seek to destroy the United States," he concluded.

‘HALO’ VIDEO GAME MUSIC COMPOSER AIMS TO REARRANGE WASHINGTON

The comments that Marty O'Donnell were criticized for were when he was commenting on the rise of Marxism, and how it has united groups that otherwise have completely different ideologies aside from a common enemy. (Alexi Rosenfeld/ Getty Images)

The comment that appeared to have caused the firestorm was when he condemned the rise of Marxism and identity politics, noting that this coalition seems to be between groups that share little in common aside from a common enemy.

"Talk about an existential threat, this is where we are right now," he said during an appearance on The WDW Pro Show. "We are on the cliff looking down into the abyss. And the abyss is Marxism, it’s anti-Western philosophy. There’s a weird alliance of all these groups who like to pretend they’re oppressed. The LGBTQ+ people, the Islamists, the Marxists, they’re all together now, acting like they’re all together on the same side. They’re not on the same side."

"Islam and communism do not mix at all," he said. "They'll be partners for a while in order to overthrow the West."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Composer Marty O'Donnell is best known for his work in the "Halo" video game series (Gabe Ginsberg/Getty Images)

Fox News Digital contacted the SacAnime convention in northern California for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Alexander Hall is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to Alexander.hall@fox.com.

articles.title: Travis Kelce says wedding to Taylor Swift was 'the best night of my life' in first official comments
articles.excerpt:
Kelce’s remarks on his marriage to Swift at Madison Square Garden comes weeks after the event, which remains shrouded in mystery

American football star Travis Kelce has described his secretive early ...
articles.body_text:
Kelce’s remarks on his marriage to Swift at Madison Square Garden comes weeks after the event, which remains shrouded in mystery

American football star Travis Kelce has described his secretive early July wedding to pop sensation Taylor Swift as “the best night of my life.”

“I appreciate everybody who came out and celebrated and, you know, had fun with us,” the Kansas City Chiefs player told a briefing.

“That’s pretty much all I’m taking away from that night. It was a crazy night. It was full of a lot of celebration.”

The couple, both 36, tied the knot over two days of celebrations at Madison Square Garden in New York on 2 and 3 July.

“It’s kind of cool to be able to, you know, live out my childhood dream of being in that venue and, you know, the mecca of all sports venues, being able to get married in there,” the three-time Super Bowl winner told a briefing.

The event remains shrouded in mystery as no images have been released. The wedding was only subsequently confirmed by a statement from Swift’s spokeswoman and a message on the giant screens of the storied concert hall and sports venue.

Little is known, other than that the ceremony was officiated by comedian-actor Adam Sandler, the couple were dressed by Jonathan Anderson for Christian Dior, and Swift wore Louboutin shoes.

A thousand people attended, including many celebrities, requiring nearby streets to be blocked off amid a heavy police presence.

The New York mayor, Zohran Mamdani, revealed that the newlyweds paid the city $160,000 to cover the resulting costs.

Journalist George Stephanopoulos said it was “so personal and so intimate” despite the venue’s cavernous size.

The head of the AMC cinema chain, Adam Aron, posted on X and then deleted a message describing the couple’s vows as “long, entertaining, personal, charming, emotional, irreverent and endearing.”

The couple made their relationship public two years ago and got engaged in August 2025.

articles.title: Birth order linked to 150 health conditions in study of 10 million American siblings
articles.excerpt: Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel analyzes a study of 10 million children indicating that birth order shapes health risks. First-born siblings show higher rates of ADHD and autism, while...
articles.body_text:
Fox News senior medical analyst Dr. Marc Siegel analyzes a study of 10 million children indicating that birth order shapes health risks. First-born siblings show higher rates of ADHD and autism, while second-born children face increased risks for migraines. Siegel joins Ainsley Earhardt to explain how parental attention and immune system development drive these stark differences.

Whether someone is the older or younger sibling may be linked to certain health outcomes later in life, according to a massive new study.

Analyzing medical data from 10 million U.S. siblings over two decades, researchers from the University of Chicago and Columbia University found links suggesting that birth order may be connected to specific long-term health risks.

Researchers examined 569 disease categories across families and among siblings, identifying 150 conditions that were significantly associated with birth order.

LONGER LIVES, WORSE HEALTH? SCIENTISTS UNCOVER TROUBLING TREND ACROSS GENERATIONS

First-born children showed a higher likelihood of neurodevelopmental and psychiatric diagnoses, including autism, ADHD, Tourette's and OCD, as well as immune-allergic conditions like food allergies.

Second-born children were statistically more prone to migraines, shingles, substance use disorders and gastrointestinal issues like gastritis.

First-born children showed higher rates of neurodevelopmental conditions such as autism, ADHD, Tourette's and OCD, as well as an increased prevalence of allergies. (iStock)

Discussing the findings on "Fox & Friends," Dr. Marc Siegel, senior medical analyst for Fox News, noted the value of such a wide-scale study.

"I love this study because it opens a lot of questions more than it gives answers, but I think I have some answers," the doctor said.

Regarding the heightened prevalence of ADHD among first-borns, Siegel offered his own hypothesis about parental behavior.

"My theory, they get more stimuli. The parents are like hovering over them, helicoptering them ... and they don't know where to look," he said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Addressing the disparities in allergic conditions, Siegel pointed to early environmental exposure, stating, "I think it's because the firstborn's immune system hasn't seen the environment before. And if it's not set properly, you get an allergy."

Differences in parental focus, early microbial exposure and maternal biological changes between pregnancies could help explain the distinct health patterns, the doctor said. (iStock)

Siegel also touched on biological and psychological factors when evaluating differences between siblings.

"I think the womb changes after you have your first child, and the second child gets a womb that's already been used. So therefore, it's more set for it," he said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Regarding the higher rate of substance use disorders among second-born children, Siegel suggested emotional drivers, saying, "it may be the same idea: 'I want attention. I'm looking for attention. I wanna do something to get a rise out of you.'"

While the research highlights patterns across a large population, the study comes with limitations.

The study highlights population-level statistical correlations, but it does not prove that birth order directly causes any specific medical condition. (iStock)

The findings demonstrate correlations rather than direct causation, meaning the trends don't necessarily stem from physiological changes, early microbial exposures or social dynamics.

Additionally, the data relies on commercial health insurance claims, which can reflect differences in diagnosis, healthcare-seeking behavior and parental attention rather than true biological functions alone.

Factors such as the age of parents between births and varying age gaps between siblings also complicate these associations. Ultimately, researchers emphasized that birth order serves as a modest population-level risk marker rather than a definitive health predictor.

The research was published in the journal Nature Health.

Khloe Quill is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital. She and the lifestyle team cover a range of story topics including food and drink, travel, and health.

articles.title: Los Angeles Lakers buyer, ex-Disney chief Bob Iger once said rooting for team was 'not in my DNA'
articles.excerpt:
DiJonai Carrington is claiming she has evidence as to why she said "white privilege". Okay, so where's the evidence?

The Los Angeles Lakers just sold for $12.5 billion to an ownership group that incl...
articles.body_text:
DiJonai Carrington is claiming she has evidence as to why she said "white privilege". Okay, so where's the evidence?

The Los Angeles Lakers just sold for $12.5 billion to an ownership group that includes a guy who once openly admitted he couldn't bring himself to root for them.

Former Disney CEO Bob Iger teamed up with Josh Kushner to buy the Lakers, which is a pretty wild turn for a guy who spent decades sitting courtside rooting for their little brother, the Clippers.

When news of the Lakers sale broke Wednesday, fans quickly resurfaced Iger's old comments about why he could never root for the team.

BOB IGER BREAKS SILENCE ON DISNEY'S SUSPENSION OF JIMMY KIMMEL OVER CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION COMMENTS

Back in January 2021, Iger explained his Lakers problem during an appearance on The Old Man and the Three podcast, hosted by none other than current Lakers head coach JJ Redick. Iger told Redick why, after moving to California in 2000, he simply couldn't bring himself to root for the Lakers.

Disney CEO Bob Iger smiles as he arrives for the the annual Allen and Co. media conference Sun Valley, Idaho July 7, 2015. REUTERS/Mike Blake - RTX1JH73 ( )

"I couldn't root for the Lakers very easily," Iger told Redick. "It just was not in my DNA."

Iger explained that growing up a New York Knicks fan made backing the Lakers an absolute non-starter.

Instead, he adopted the Clippers to get his basketball fix. His other reason for picking the Clippers over LA's powerhouse was even simpler: price.

JOSH HART CALLS FINALS TICKET PRICES AT MADISON SQUARE GARDEN 'RIDICULOUS' AS FANS PRICED OUT BEFORE GAME 3

Iger explicitly told Redick that "their seats were a lot cheaper than the Lakers."

Los Angeles Lakers' Governor Jeanie Buss appears as the Lakers host a 2021-2022 season kick-off event to unveil and announce a new global marketing partnership with Bibigo, which will appear on the Lakers' jersey at the UCLA Health Training Center in El Segundo on Monday, Sept. 20, 2021. (Getty Images)

The man who just helped buy the Lakers for $12.5 billion originally chose the Clippers because the tickets were cheaper. Iger once said rooting for the purple and gold wasn't in his DNA.

The timing of the blockbuster deal is where things get even more interesting. Billionaire Mark Walter agreed to buy the Buss family's controlling stake in June 2025 at a roughly $10 billion valuation. Just 14 months later, he's flipping the Lakers for $12.5 billion.

That lightning-fast turnaround comes as Walter's business empire reportedly faces federal scrutiny, including questions surrounding billions of dollars in private-credit investments. There's no evidence the investigation forced the sale — or that Walter suddenly needed cash — but unloading the Lakers barely a year after buying them certainly makes the timing interesting.

As for Iger, he clearly has the resources to help purchase the franchise. But for a guy who once said rooting for the Lakers wasn't in his DNA, becoming one of their owners is one hell of a plot twist.

The Walt Disney Company Chairman and CEO Bob Iger and President of Marvel Studios and producer Kevin Feige attend the Los Angeles World Premiere of Marvel Studios' "Captain Marvel" at Dolby Theatre on March 4, 2019, in Hollywood, California. (Photo by Alberto E. Rodriguez/Getty Images for Disney) (Alberto E. Rodriguez/Getty Images for Disney)

Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

Alejandro Avila is a longtime writer at OutKick, living in Southern California.

articles.title: Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders give Browns a preseason quarterback battle worth watching
articles.excerpt:
Dan says the Shedeur Sanders & Colorado luster has finally gone away after Deshaun Watson is expected to be the Browns starting quarterback after minicamp

The NFL preseason is generally a tough sell....
articles.body_text:
Dan says the Shedeur Sanders & Colorado luster has finally gone away after Deshaun Watson is expected to be the Browns starting quarterback after minicamp

The NFL preseason is generally a tough sell. Fans are excited that football is back, sure, but then the starters play a series or two, and a bunch of guys who aren't going to make the roster finish the game.

But the Cleveland Browns just gave us two reasons to pay attention to their first two preseason games.

RAIDERS' NO. 1 PICK FERNANDO MENDOZA WILL GET 'PLENTY OF EXPERIENCE' IN PRESEASON DEBUT THURSDAY

Head coach Todd Monken informed his quarterbacks Wednesday afternoon that Deshaun Watson will start Cleveland's preseason opener Saturday in Chicago against the Bears. Monken also plans to start Shedeur Sanders in the Browns' second preseason game, at home against the Buffalo Bills on Aug. 22.

Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders will each get preseason starts as the Browns try to settle one of the NFL's most intriguing quarterback battles. (Diamond Images/Getty Images)

Monken said the plan is for Watson and Sanders to play roughly a half apiece against Chicago, then flip the order the following week against Buffalo.

Cleveland has spent the offseason treating its quarterback job like an actual competition, and Monken has backed that up with how he's handled practice. Watson and Sanders have alternated days working with the first-team offense during training camp after both received opportunities with the starters during the spring.

But preseason football is where that competition finally becomes something the rest of us can actually evaluate.

FALCONS QUARTERBACK COMPETITION TAKES EARLY HIT AS TUA TAGOVAILOA SUFFERS 'FLARE-UP' IN TRAINING CAMP

Watson gets the first crack, and his start against Chicago carries plenty of weight even if Monken isn't ready to call anyone QB1. Watson hasn't appeared in an NFL game since rupturing his Achilles in October 2024. He later needed a second surgery after re-rupturing the tendon and didn't play at all last season.

So, watching Watson take an actual snap against an opposing defense is going to be a little more interesting than the standard August opener.

The Browns don't just need to know whether Watson can operate Monken's offense. They need to see whether he still resembles an NFL starting quarterback after nearly two years without playing in a game. He's obviously not the player the Browns traded three first-round picks to obtain in March 2022.

Watson led the NFL in passing yards in 2020, then didn't play at all in 2021 after requesting a trade. During that time, dozens of massage therapists accused him of sexual misconduct, further complicating his situation in Houston. The final two civil lawsuits tied to those allegations were dismissed earlier this year.

None of it stopped the Browns from trading for Watson in what might be the worst trade in NFL history. The 30-year-old quarterback has started 19 games in the past four seasons, compiling a 9-10 record.

Deshaun Watson hasn't started an NFL game for the Cleveland Browns since 2024. (Jason Miller/Getty Images)

Cleveland doesn't need Watson to be the guy who was considered one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL. They just need him to prove he can still be a competent QB.

Then there's the 24-year-old Sanders, who slid to the Browns in the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft. Sanders wasn't even the first quarterback drafted by the Browns; that was Dillon Gabriel in the third round. Gabriel is still on the roster and technically part of the team's competition to be the starter, but appears to be behind Watson and Sanders. They also drafted Taylen Green in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft.

BROWNS DRAFT ANOTHER QUARTERBACK, MAKING SHEDEUR SANDERS' STARTING JOB EVEN LESS SECURE

Unlike Watson, Sanders has recent game tape, and plenty of it. The second-year QB appeared in eight games as a rookie and started seven, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. There were flashes of promise, most notably a 364-yard, three-touchdown performance against Tennessee, but there were also the mistakes you'd expect from a young quarterback trying to figure out the NFL.

That's what makes this battle so intriguing. Not only is Sanders technically the incumbent, but he comes with a ton of hype thanks to his bravado and last name. He's already started meaningful NFL games, showed enough to make the Browns curious about what comes next and has now had a full offseason under a new head coach to make his case.

Usually, there's an obvious answer to a QB "competition" and teams just go through the motions. But this feels like a true battle for the starting gig. Giving Watson and Sanders their own preseason starts makes it pretty clear Monken wants to see both guys in game action with the first-team offense.

More importantly, Cleveland has created something that's usually missing from August football: stakes that people actually care about.

Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders started 7 games in 2025. (AP Photo/Sue Ogrocki)

Nobody is going to remember who wins Browns-Bears on Saturday. Nobody should. But if Watson looks sharp, moves well and pushes the ball downfield, that's meaningful. If he looks tentative or rusty after such a long layoff, that's meaningful too.

The same applies to Sanders against Buffalo. He'll get a home crowd that already knows him, and every good throw is going to add fuel to the idea that he should be Cleveland's starter now and into the future. Every bad decision will be a reminder that his rookie season was uneven for a reason.

Monken doesn't have to name a regular-season starter after either game. In fact, he probably shouldn't unless someone makes the decision obvious.

Cleveland still has a third preseason game against New England on Aug. 27, so there's room to keep evaluating before the real games begin. And if Monken really wants to mess with everyone, he could even throw Gabriel a start in that contest.

For now, Watson gets Chicago. Sanders gets Buffalo. And for two Saturdays, Cleveland's quarterback competition becomes one of the most interesting things the NFL preseason has to offer.
